questions.prompt: A learner has a weighted total of 93 and a completed stretch, but one CAP03 gate check fails. What is the verdict?
options: Distinction, because the total is above 90 and the stretch is done.
Not graduated: a failed gate blocks graduation regardless of the total.
Merit, because failed gates only reduce the grade by one level.
Pass, after the stretch is converted into bonus points on the failed gate.
questions.explanation: Gates are conditions of graduation; neither the total nor a stretch can compensate for a failed gate.

questions.prompt: Milestone scores 95, 86.5, 81, 84, 75.5, 70, 84, 86.5, 92.5 for CAP01 to CAP09 with the official weights (8, 12, 12, 11, 13, 12, 10, 14, 8). Weighted total.
questions.explanation: Sum of weight times score divided by 100 = 83.1.

questions.prompt: Why should every number in the Results section come from a placeholder resolved from metrics.json?
options: It makes the report shorter and easier to read.
Hand-typed numbers are less accurate than automatic ones because humans cannot read decimals.
Journals require placeholders in the submitted source.
After a rerun a hand-typed number can silently disagree with the logs; a placeholder cannot.
questions.explanation: The goal is that the report and the logs cannot drift apart; unknown keys fail the build.

questions.prompt: The smoke test reruns six seeds in a fresh container and seed 1003 ends with a different outcome. What does this tell you?
options: Something in the pipeline is non-deterministic or the environment differs; the release is not reproducible yet.
The test is too strict; accept a 10 % mismatch rate.
The stored file is wrong by definition because the fresh run is newer.
Nothing, because six seeds are too few to say anything.
questions.explanation: The smoke test requires identical outcomes on the stored seeds; find the source of variation.

questions.prompt: Minimum number of references (each with a URL or DOI) required by the CAP09 acceptance test.
Which sentence is calibrated for a project that was only run in MuJoCo?
options: Our robot solves household tidying in the real world.
Our robot closes the sim-to-real gap.
In simulation, 94 of 120 episodes succeeded (Wilson interval 70 to 85 %); no real robot was tested.
The robot is safe because the supervisor passed all tests.
questions.explanation: State what was measured, with an interval, and what was not tested.

questions.prompt: List what a clean-checkout dry run of the release must check before you tag v1.0.
rubric: Clones into an empty directory and builds the image or fresh environment from the lock file.
Runs reproduce-smoke without network access and compares outcomes with the stored file.
Runs the full test suite and lint, with a clean working tree before tagging.
Records time and every defect found, and states what observation would show non-reproducibility.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
